headline: Medium-risk pair: Khoj can read shared notes while langchain4j can be wired to act on them, creating default-path leakage and miscoordination risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports RAG plus optional web search, so attacker-controlled content in shared notes can influence its outputs. langchain4j is a framework that can consume those outputs in downstream apps. No shared channel is explicit, so this is inferred from file-based ingestion rather than proven direct bridging.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through the same note corpus or exported files
IF langchain4j-based code treats Khoj output as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a read-only, curated corpus
Add provenance tags to retrieved passages
Strip instruction-like text before passing outputs to langchain4j
Use a human review step for any tool-triggering text
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters in the orchestration layer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj explicitly reads indexed personal notes/files and handles model-provider API keys for self-hosted use, while langchain4j is a library that can be embedded in apps that may forward prompts to external models. The pair can therefore move sensitive notes into a broader application path unless the integration is tightly constrained.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes personal notes that contain sensitive data
IF a langchain4j integration forwards those retrieved notes to a third-party model or logging sink
mitigations: Limit the indexed corpus to non-sensitive documents
Disable or redact logs in the langchain4j app
Use local-only models for the integration
Rotate and scope any API keys used by Khoj
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access and no write or git capabilities, while langchain4j has no declared runtime capabilities because it is a library. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main risk is only if an external app built on langchain4j adds writes, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF a separate langchain4j host application adds filesystem or git writes
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep Khoj on a read-only mount
Avoid sharing writable working directories
Serialize any external writes through one owner process
Document ownership of each resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and docs, and langchain4j is commonly used to build downstream agents that may act on upstream text. If the integration treats Khoj output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect support actions or generated responses. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF langchain4j consumes Khoj answers without verification
IF downstream code turns those answers into customer-facing replies or actions
mitigations: Require citation-backed answers from Khoj
Add a verification prompt before acting on retrieved text
Use confidence thresholds to block low-confidence outputs
Log and review disputed answers
requires-engineering: implement a validation layer between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, which can include regulated data, while langchain4j is an open-source library with no declared residency or retention controls. The compliance gap is therefore about deployment choices around the library, not an inherent violation by Khoj alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is indexed in Khoj
IF the langchain4j application stores or transmits that data under a different retention or residency policy
mitigations: Classify the data before indexing
Keep regulated data out of the integration path
Align retention settings across both systems
Review deployment region and logging destinations
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
